T01_remote_contract.title: Write the remote contract of record (docs/REMOTE.md + shared types)
T01_remote_contract.instruction:
Goal: turn the plan (docs/plans/draft/iphone-remote.md, sections 3.1-3.7) into the precise contract every later node implements, and resolve the open decisions it lists.

Steps:
1. Re-verify the coupling points in section 1 of the plan against the code (src/main/index.ts, session-host.ts, bridge.ts, src/renderer/src/state/app.ts, state/atp.ts, lib/session.ts). Correct the plan where the code differs.
2. Write docs/REMOTE.md: HostCore method table shape (name, validate, run(ctx,args), scope desktop-only vs remote), the full method list grouped by area (chat, stores, atp, browser, computer, fs, uploads, devices, remote, settings, auth, github, update) with which existing IPC channel each replaces or wraps; EventHub topics (global, chat:<handle>), event envelope {bootId, seq, topic, event}, snapshot envelope {seq, value}, ring buffer bounds, resync rules; idempotency (header, cache scope and TTL, host_restarted error); RPC allowlist; dialog first-wins and dialog_resolved; leases and dispose rule; store rev/baseRev conflicts; error model (HTTP status + {code, message}); SSE framing (id: bootId:seq), heartbeat, subscription endpoint; auth (cookie, pairing states, Host/Origin/CSRF/Tailscale-User-Login checks, revocation); static app/CSP. Record a decision for each open decision in plan section 7 (port, QR, cross-device revoke, keep-awake default, update restart, scopes); leave Web Push to T38.
3. Add src/shared/host-api.ts with the TypeScript types only (envelopes, error codes, method names/arg/result types, HostEvent additions such as dialog_resolved, lease events, attention summary). No runtime behavior yet; a small vitest test for any pure helper you add (e.g. parsing 'bootId:seq').

Deliverables: docs/REMOTE.md, src/shared/host-api.ts (+ test if helpers).
Acceptance: every method later nodes need is named with types; every decision recorded with its reason; typecheck and tests pass.
T01_remote_contract.context: Project: pi-gna (Electron 44 desktop UI for the pi coding agent, macOS; repo /Users/manuelcecchetto/Code/personal/pi-gna). Epic: iPhone remote access: a mobile web app/PWA with feature parity (not identical layout) with the desktop app, used from Safari or the Home Screen over Tailscale (tailscale serve, HTTPS, tailnet only), controlling the pi-gna running on the host Mac. Agents, tools, repositories, the browser and Computer Use stay on the host. Read first: docs/plans/draft/iphone-remote.md (the plan of record: coupling points with file:line evidence, feature inventory, design sections 3.1-3.7, risks, non-goals) and docs/DESIGN.md (architecture, conventions, 'Verifying the UI'). Once T01 exists, docs/REMOTE.md is the contract of record and wins over the plan where they differ. Key decisions: the desktop renderer is NOT rewritten (it keeps IPC and local reduction of events); one HostCore method table in main is dispatched by both IPC and the remote server; orchestration that today lives in the renderer (ATP runner, card/lament/review chat setups, queue ops) moves to Electron main, not to pi extensions (extensions stay for agent-facing tools); the AgentBridge stays loopback-only and is never exposed; no raw RPC passthrough remotely. Constraints: closing or suspending a client never cancels host work; no unauthenticated listener; remote access off by default; never copy host credentials to the phone; no privileged sleep hacks; no native iOS app. Conventions: TypeScript; main and preload import only Node and Electron (no runtime npm dependencies; renderer/mobile code may bundle devDependencies through Vite); pure helpers in src/shared with vitest tests; comment density like surrounding code; update docs/DESIGN.md for behavior changes and add a CHANGELOG.md Unreleased line for user-visible changes. Verification for every code node: `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass; do not weaken tests. UI checks use test instances exactly as docs/DESIGN.md 'Verifying the UI' says (own PIGNA_USER_DATA, PIGNA_BACKGROUND=1, own free debugging port, scripts/fake-pi.mjs via PIGNA_PI_BIN, stop by PID, never pkill patterns, never touch the user's running pi-gna). Commit your node's work as one commit.
T01_remote_contract.report:
## Outcome
docs/REMOTE.md (contract of record) and src/shared/host-api.ts (types + pure helpers) written; test src/shared/host-api.test.ts added. All plan section 7 decisions recorded except Web Push (left to T38).

## Facts Learned
- Plan coupling points all hold; line numbers drifted slightly (registerIpc handlers index.ts:228-380, stores :101-125) – corrected in REMOTE.md section 0.
- Plan missed that `send` in state/app.ts:410 composes card block, annotations, file mentions and images in the renderer, so `chat.send` must compose host-side.
- SessionState/reducer live in src/renderer/src/lib/session.ts; shared code cannot import it, so host-api.ts has opaque `SessionStateJson` until T05 moves the reducer to src/shared/session-state.ts.

## Decisions Made
Port 4517 (loopback, editable); QR via renderer-bundled encoder plus always URL+code text; any paired device may revoke single devices (not pair/enable/revoke-all); keep-awake default "while a chat or plan runs"; update Restart desktop-only; no scopes in v1 (DeviceInfo.scope reserved "full"). Also: one object arg per method; `providers.*` replaces preload `auth.*`; ATP low-level methods desktop-only until T23; chat.rawCommand desktop-only transition; subscriptions never lease; coarse baseRev conflicts first. Ring 2000 events/8 MiB; idempotency TTL 10 min/1000 per device, X-Pigna-Boot header gives host_restarted; lease grace 60 s; pairing code 8 chars/5 min/5 attempts.

## Files Touched
docs/REMOTE.md, src/shared/host-api.ts, src/shared/host-api.test.ts

## Interfaces Changed
New types only: HostMethods (name -> args/result), EventEnvelope/Snapshot, HostEvent (+dialog_resolved, lease, closed), GlobalEvent, HostError/HOST_ERROR_STATUS, RPC_ALLOWLIST/isAllowedRpc, DESKTOP_ONLY_METHODS/methodScope/methodMutates, formatEventId/parseEventId/planReplay, constants (RING_*, HEARTBEAT_MS, REMOTE_CSP, pairing limits), Revved<T>, UiState, DeviceInfo, RemoteStatus. No runtime behavior wired.

## Verification
pnpm typecheck: pass. pnpm test: 47 files, 404 tests pass (includes new host-api tests).

## Risks
Types for some results (atp.claim/head/commit) are `unknown` placeholders until T23; `browser.layout` args unknown. `Revved<T>` assumes stores can add `rev` without breaking existing value shapes (T09). DESIGN.md/CHANGELOG not updated (no behavior change yet).

## Recommended Next Step
T02/T03 spikes, then T04 EventHub implementing envelopes/ring/planReplay from host-api.ts.

T02_spike_browser_frames.title: Spike: browser frame source for remote viewers while the window is hidden
T02_spike_browser_frames.instruction:
Goal: decide how the host streams a browser tab to a phone, measured, before T35 builds it.

Context: BrowserManager (src/main/browser/manager.ts) attaches WebContentsView tabs to the app window; DESIGN.md (Browser) records that capturePage/sendInputEvent fail when the window is hidden because Chromium stops compositing, and that CDP Page.captureScreenshot and CDP input work. A phone may view a tab while the desktop window is hidden, occluded, minimized or the pane is closed (the tab's view detached).

Steps:
1. Write a throwaway spike script under scripts/ (like scripts/responsive-spike.mjs) that runs a test instance or a bare Electron app with a WebContentsView and a local animated fixture page.
2. Measure for each state (visible, window hidden, occluded, view detached from the window, emulated mobile viewport): (a) CDP Page.startScreencast frames per second and whether frames arrive at all; (b) Page.captureScreenshot polling latency and fps at quality 60, scaled to 390x844@3x and @2x; (c) bytes per frame; (d) whether CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent/dispatchTouchEvent/insertText work in each state; (e) whether BrowserManager.ensureVisible-like attaching is needed.
3. Record results and the recommended approach (and fallback) in a 'Remote browser' section of docs/REMOTE.md if it exists, else docs/RESPONSIVE_BROWSER.md's style in a new docs/REMOTE_BROWSER_SPIKE.md that T35 reads.

Deliverables: spike script, measurements table, recommendation.
Acceptance: numbers for every state; a clear choice for T35 with its limits. No production code changes.

T03_ios_constraints.title: Research and record iOS Safari/Home Screen constraints for the PWA

Steps:
1. Research with primary sources (WebKit blog/bugs, Apple developer docs, MDN) and note iOS versions: Home Screen web apps' storage separate from Safari (WebKit bug 181849); cookie persistence and the 17.x session-cookie reset reports (bug 272325); ITP 7-day cap and its Home Screen exemption; EventSource behavior on suspension and reconnection; service worker scope and update behavior; manifest fields iOS honors (display standalone, icons, apple-touch-icon, status bar style); safe-area insets and visualViewport with the keyboard; file input for photos/camera/Files; clipboard API limits; Web Push requirements (16.4+, Home Screen only, permission on user gesture); memory/process limits for iframes (inline visuals).
2. If Xcode's iOS Simulator is installed (`xcrun simctl list devices`), load a minimal local test page (python3 -m http.server is fine) with `xcrun simctl openurl` to confirm what can be observed there (standalone mode needs manual Add to Home Screen: note it). Do not install anything.
3. Write docs/REMOTE_IOS.md: each constraint, its source link, the design consequence for pi-gna (pairing inside the installed app, persistent cookie, reconnect triggers, SW caches only the shell, etc.), and what only a real device can confirm (feed into T21's runbook).

Acceptance: every constraint has a source and a consequence; no code changes.

T04_event_hub.title: Add EventHub: sequenced topics, ring buffer, resync, desktop subscriber
T04_event_hub.instruction:
Goal: replace the single-window send() fan-out (src/main/index.ts:89) with an EventHub so several clients can receive host pushes with sequence numbers and replay.

Steps:
1. Implement src/main/event-hub.ts per docs/REMOTE.md: bootId (random per launch), monotonic seq, publish(topic, event), subscribers with topic filters, a ring buffer bounded by count and bytes, since(bootId, seq) returning the gap or a resync marker, and per-subscriber close.
2. Route every existing push through the hub: session batches (IPC.events), board/laments/settings/computer changes, atp plans/held, browser state/reveal/annotation, auth updates, update state. The desktop window is one subscriber that receives exactly what it receives today over the same IPC channels (no renderer change in this node). Window-only UI pushes (menu toggles, window focus, open-project) may stay direct sends: say which in a comment and in docs/REMOTE.md.
3. Unit tests: ordering, topic filtering, ring eviction by count and by bytes, replay of a gap, resync when the cursor is too old or the bootId differs, subscriber removal.

Acceptance: desktop behavior unchanged (run a fake-pi test instance and confirm streaming, board pushes and browser state still update); tests pass.

T06_session_registry.title: Make SessionHost a registry: host handles, file dedupe, leases, snapshots
T06_session_registry.instruction:
Goal: the host, not a window, owns which chats are live, who is attached, and their authoritative state.

Steps:
1. Host-issued handles: open returns a handle generated in main (keep the HANDLE format). Opening a session file that is already live returns the existing handle and attaches the caller instead of spawning a second pi (DESIGN.md pi RPC notes: two pi processes on one file are unsafe).
2. Leases: attach(handle, client) / detach(handle, client). A pi process stops only on explicit close, or when it has no leases and the shared isDisposable rule holds (not prompted, not running, not compacting, no dialogs, no unread outcome). Explicit close is broadcast. Keep ATP chats' and background chats' rules (they are opened without a viewer: model this as a host-held lease released by the owning task).
3. Authoritative state: per handle, run the shared reducer over hydrate(entries) and every host event, timestamped by the host; expose snapshot(handle, {beforeTurn?, turns}) returning {seq, state} paged by user turns; keep the reducer cheap for streaming deltas.
4. Attention summary for all live chats (running, waiting for you, failed, last settle outcome and time) published on the global topic when it changes.
5. Presence: which clients are viewing which chat (from attach and a client 'viewing' signal), for later 'close when done' and unread rules.
6. Tests: dedupe, lease lifecycle and dispose rule, explicit close broadcast, snapshot paging, snapshot+events equals live reduction.

Acceptance: unit tests pass; no renderer change yet besides compiling (T08 adapts the desktop).

T07_command_semantics.title: Add command semantics: idempotency, RPC allowlist, per-chat mutex, dialogs first-wins
T07_command_semantics.instruction:
Goal: commands from several clients are safe to retry, ordered, and cannot answer the same approval twice.

Steps:
1. Command layer in main: optional idempotency key per call; cache (bootId,key) -> result for 10 minutes per chat/store; a retry returns the cached result; an unknown key from a previous bootId fails with code host_restarted (per docs/REMOTE.md).
2. RPC allowlist for client commands (docs/REMOTE.md list). The desktop keeps using the same path; remote callers get the allowlist enforced (callers are tagged in ctx). Refuse bash and new_session remotely.
3. Per-chat async mutex; host methods chat.interrupt (clear_queue then abort, returning restored texts to the caller) and chat.editQueue (port editQueue/applyQueueOp from src/renderer/src/state/app.ts:549 and lib/queue.ts; move applyQueueOp to src/shared) run under it.
4. Dialogs: record every extension_ui_request dialog (select/confirm/input/editor) and main's own requestChoice ids per chat; respondDialog(handle, response, ctx): first answer wins, emit dialog_resolved {id, by}, later answers fail with already_answered; pi timeouts, chat exit and settleChoices clear them. Snapshots include pending dialogs.
5. Tests for each: retry dedupe, host_restarted, allowlist refusal, interrupt/editQueue atomicity under concurrent calls, double answer.

Acceptance: tests pass; existing computer-use approval tests (src/main/computer/agent.test.ts, route.integration.test.ts) still pass.

## Outcome
Command semantics are in main. IdempotencyCache and KeyedMutex (src/main/command-layer.ts); SessionHost enforces the RPC allowlist for remote callers, serializes chat edits, and tracks dialogs first-answer-wins. Tests pass.
## Facts Learned
- Renderer's `respondDialog` removes its card optimistically, so a desktop answer that loses the race is swallowed in index.ts (HostError ignored); the card goes on dialog_resolved anyway.
- computer approval tests unaffected (full suite green).
## Decisions Made
- IdempotencyCache.run(scope, key, seenBoot, fingerprint, fn): host_restarted when seenBoot differs from bootId (before running); same-key different fingerprint -> bad_request idempotency_mismatch; 10 min TTL, LRU 1000/scope, results >256KiB -> conflict result_unavailable on retry; failures not cached. Scope is chosen by the caller (HostCore: device/method).
- Mutex (KeyedMutex per handle) wraps interrupt, editQueue and the prompt/steer/follow_up/clear_queue/abort commands; other commands (compact, get_*) are unlocked so a long compact does not block.
- Dialogs: Live.dialogs (pending, with timer mirroring pi's `timeout`) + `resolved` set (200) so a late answer gives already_answered, unknown id gives not_found. Exit emits dialog_resolved outcome "exit" for each pending dialog before the exit event. respondUi replaced by respondDialog(handle, response, ctx) which throws HostError.
- Computer-use/browser approval answers log the answering device.
- Added HostCtx and actorOf to host-api.ts. command(handle, command, ctx = desktop) rejects with scope_denied outside the allowlist for non-desktop callers.

src/main/command-layer.ts (+test), src/main/session-host.ts (+test), src/main/index.ts, src/shared/host-api.ts, src/shared/queue.ts (moved from renderer lib/queue.ts), renderer imports (app.ts, QueueCard.tsx, lib.test.ts).
## Interfaces Changed
SessionHost: command(handle, cmd, ctx?), interrupt(handle): string[], editQueue(handle, op): boolean, respondDialog(handle, response, ctx?) (replaces respondUi). host-api: HostCtx, actorOf. applyQueueOp now at src/shared/queue.ts.

## Outcome
Desktop renderer now coexists with remote clients: IPC gained detach/attach(snapshot)/viewing/liveChats/attention/interrupt/editQueue/respondDialog; app.ts uses them. UI unchanged.
## Facts Learned
- SessionHost already attached the desktop lease on open and honored the renderer's provisional handle; only reuse (file already live) returns another handle.
- ipc.ts HostEvent was narrower than host-api's; it is now re-exported from host-api so the renderer sees dialog_resolved/lease/closed.

- interrupt/editQueue delegate to SessionHost (atomic per chat); renderer keeps only a cheap running/compacting guard.
- Chats started elsewhere: adopted (attachSession -> snapshot, events buffered and filtered by seq) when their attention summary is non-idle and they are unknown; reload adopts all live chats then reuses a launch-folder draft or opens a new one. A `closed` event by another client removes the chat.
- Window reports `viewing` to the host (store subscription + focus) so host unread/attention clear.
- Opening a file already live under another handle: provisional session is dropped and the host's chat adopted (callers of start() holding the provisional handle would go stale; only possible for resumes of live files).

## Outcome
JsonStore (board, laments, settings, computer, github) now carries a monotonic `rev` and checks optional `baseRev` on free-text ops. Desktop sends baseRev; conflicts reload and toast.
## Facts Learned
- `Revved<T>` already existed in host-api.ts; the pure shared types stay unrevved, rev is added by JsonStore (persisted as a `rev` key; missing = 0; incremented only when apply changes the value; refused ops and no-ops don't bump it).
- Per-field detection was cheap: JsonStore keeps the last 64 values by rev (immutable, structurally shared) and the model's optional `conflicts(base, current, op)` compares only the field the op replaces. Base older than 64 revisions counts as conflict for text edits.
- `move` to the same column and edit with the same text still bump rev (updatedAt/array changes).
- atp.test.ts "shows a plan the architect writes" is flaky under load (failed once, passes in reruns).

- Text ops that conflict: board `edit` (title/notes/tags), settings `theme`/`wallpaper`/`model`. Laments and Computer have no text-replacing op (rev only). Everything else last-writer-wins.
- Conflict = HostError("conflict", "Conflict: this <store> changed elsewhere ...", {rev}); over IPC only the message survives, renderer detects the "Conflict:" prefix (editError in app.ts).
- Renderer: optimistic boards keep `before.rev`; applyBoard(op, baseRev?) defaults to the window's rev; CardDialog tracks the rev its title/notes came from (editedFrom) and, on refusal, reloads the saved values. TagEditor/AddCard use the default.
- GithubStore also persists a rev (unused); SettingsStore interface in github.ts is now a plain interface returning unrevved values.

T10_host_lifecycle.instruction:
Goal: when remote access is on, the Mac keeps serving with the window closed and does not idle-sleep, without promising unsupported closed-lid operation.

Steps:
1. Settings (src/shared/settings.ts, applySettingsOp + tests): remote.enabled (default false), remote.port (default per docs/REMOTE.md), remote.keepAwake ('off' | 'while-working' | 'always', default per docs/REMOTE.md), openAtLogin.
2. src/main/index.ts: while remote.enabled, closing the window hides it (window-all-closed must not quit; Dock activate shows it); Quit asks for confirmation when paired devices or running chats exist. BrowserManager keeps working because the window still exists.
3. Keep-awake: powerSaveBlocker.start('prevent-app-suspension') per setting ('while-working' = any chat running or ATP plan running); stop it when not needed; log transitions.
4. Open at login: app.setLoginItemSettings.
5. Settings UI copy (desktop, a 'Remote access' section stub that T14 completes): keep-awake prevents idle sleep only; a closed MacBook lid sleeps unless on power with an external display (clamshell); for laptop-independent use, run pi-gna on an always-on Mac.
6. Tests for settings ops; manual check in a test instance that close hides and reopen shows.

Acceptance: behavior only changes when remote.enabled is on; tests pass.

T13_remote_server.title: Build RemoteServer: authenticated HTTP API, SSE with replay, static app
T13_remote_server.instruction:
Goal: the only network surface for remote clients, implemented with node:http (no dependencies).

Steps:
1. src/main/remote-server.ts: listen on 127.0.0.1:<remote.port> only while remote.enabled; stop on disable/quit.
2. Middleware order for every request: Host must equal the configured tailnet name (from T14's tailscale status, or a setting; reject others), body size limits, device cookie auth (DeviceStore) on everything except the app shell, /api/hello and /api/pair/*; mutating requests require same-origin Origin and X-Pigna-Client: 1; Tailscale-User-Login must be present and match the device's paired login. Never accept AgentBridge tokens.
3. POST /api/call/<method>: dispatch to the HostCore table with ctx {client: device id}, refusing desktop-only methods; Idempotency-Key header passed to the command layer; JSON errors {code, message} with the statuses in docs/REMOTE.md.
4. GET /api/events (SSE): id bootId:seq, Last-Event-ID replay from the EventHub or a resync event, heartbeat comments every 15 s, per-stream subscriptions (POST /api/subscribe {stream, chats}), backpressure (stop writing above a writableLength cap, then resync or close), stream closed at once when its device is revoked.
5. Static: serve out/mobile (built by T16; until then a placeholder) with a strict CSP header and cache headers; /api/hello returns {bootId, build}. Pairing endpoints: claim code, poll pending status, receive Set-Cookie on approval.
6. Audit log line per call: device id, method, status (no payloads).
7. Integration tests with node http client: auth required, replay and resync, heartbeat, backpressure, revoked stream closes, desktop-only refused.

Acceptance: tests pass; with remote off nothing listens.

T15_security_tests.title: Security test suite for the remote surface
T15_security_tests.instruction:
Goal: lock the security boundaries with tests before any mobile UI ships.

Steps (src/main/remote-server.security.test.ts or similar, node http client against a server with fakes):

## Outcome
src/mobile/client/host-client.ts: `HostClient` (call + SSE stream + store). 13 unit tests with fake EventSource/fetch/timers.
## Facts Learned
- Native EventSource cannot set Last-Event-ID on a fresh instance; only the browser's own auto-reconnect (readyState CONNECTING) sends it. So error with CONNECTING waits for the browser (gap replays); watchdog/visibility/pageshow/online create a new EventSource, which the server answers with `resync` (no replay). Server has no query fallback.
- EventSource exposes no HTTP status: on failure the client probes /api/hello to tell unauthorized / outdated / unreachable.
## Decisions Made
- Keys: every methodMutates method gets one Idempotency-Key per call, reused on retries; transient (unavailable/rate_limited/internal, network) retried 3x with backoff for keyed calls AND reads; host_restarted/conflict/etc never retried. 401 -> state unauthorized + onUnauthorized.
- Store (renderer createStore, needs rAF) holds `connection`, `bootId`, `lastSeq`, `global` (projects, attention, board, laments, settings, computer, ui, atp, browser) and `chats[handle]` = SessionState reduced with shared `reduceHostEvent`.
- Events <= lastSeq dropped; boot change -> resync resets lastSeq. During snapshot reads events are buffered per topic and applied if seq > snapshot seq (reads without seq, e.g. chat.list, use lastSeq at fetch start).
- States: connecting, live (on hello), reconnecting, unreachable (>=3 failures, keeps retrying, state kept), unauthorized/outdated (client stops).
- `setChats(handles)` POSTs /api/subscribe (sent directly, no idempotency key) and loads chat.snapshot; stream URL carries chats on reconnect. Does not lease (chat.attach is the UI's call).

New `HostClient` {store, streamId, call, start, stop, setChats, resync}, `Env`, `browserEnv()`, `ClientState`.

The phone can now do the vertical slice against a live host: Projects -> Chats -> Chat, open an existing session, send (steer while running), Queue as follow-up, Stop (confirm, queued texts restored to the composer), stream, approval cards, and recover after a connection drop. The desktop window of the same instance showed the same chat (shared transcript, "Interrupted" run) after the phone's actions.

## Facts Learned
- The T17 HostClient posted `/api/<method>`, but RemoteServer (T13) serves `/api/call/<method>`: nothing worked end to end. Fixed in the client (+ docs).
- host-core's chat methods had drifted from host-api.ts types (`chat.open` takes `{request}` and returns `entries`; `chat.interrupt` returns `string[]`; `chat.respondDialog` returns a `DialogAnswer`; `chat.snapshot`, `app.info` did not exist in the table though the client and types used them; `chat.live`/`chat.viewing` existed but were not in `HostMethods`). Types now match the table; REMOTE.md rows updated.
- A browser-retried EventSource reuses its first URL, so a stream opened before a chat was on screen comes back without the chat subscription (events stop silently, replay only covers held topics). Fixed: on `hello` with the same boot the client re-subscribes and rereads the chats (unit tested).
- Mobile Tailwind only scanned `src/mobile`; the shared components' utilities (max-w-[78%], touch:*) were missing from the mobile CSS until `@source` for `renderer/src/components` and `lib` was added.
- fake-pi reported its own temp session file even for `--session <file>`, so attention `sessionPath` never matched the list; it now echoes `--session` (still never writes it).
- Browser pane: cookie via `document.cookie` did not stick on the proxy origin; the throwaway proxy (/tmp/t19/proxy.mjs, not committed) injects the device cookie, `Tailscale-User-Login`, https Origin and loopback Host. The device was seeded into `remote-devices.json` instead of pairing.

## Decisions Made
- Shared components stay shared via a `ChatUi` React context (`src/renderer/src/lib/chat-ui.tsx`: state slice + actions: setExpanded, openLightbox, showBoard, openExternal, respondDialog, editQueue, homeDir). Desktop provides it in `renderer/src/main.tsx` from its store/window.studio; mobile from `src/mobile/chat-ui.ts`. `compaction.test.ts` mocks the new hooks like it mocked `useApp`.
- Added `touch:` Tailwind variant (`pointer: coarse`) for touch sizing in Dialogs and the user bubble; hover timestamps hidden on touch; `Transcript` takes an optional `earlier` prop (`{count, load}`) for host paging with a scroll anchor.
- `chat.open` strips `entries` for remote callers (phone reads `chat.snapshot`, 40 turns, `before` cursor); `AttentionSummary.sessionPath` added to match live chats to list rows; `chat.live` added to READ_ONLY; `app.info` implemented (`HostDeps.app`).
- Pure helpers in `src/mobile/chat-list.ts` (reuses `projectViews`, so order is the sidebar's) and `drafts.ts`, with tests. Drafts: `localStorage` `pigna:draft:<session file>`.
- Sign out moved to the Projects footer; `onUnauthorized` now returns to Pairing. A reload inside a chat lands on Projects.

T20_slice_e2e.title: Automated end-to-end test of the vertical slice
T20_slice_e2e.instruction:
Goal: a repeatable script proving pairing, open, prompt, streaming, approvals, cancellation and reconnect recovery without a phone.

Steps:
1. scripts/remote-slice-e2e.mjs: start a test instance (own profile/port, PIGNA_PI_BIN = fake-pi wrapper with an extension that raises ctx.ui.confirm), enable remote access through settings in the profile, pair client A and client B through the API (approve via CDP on the test window or a test hook guarded to test profiles only), open an existing session file, prompt from A, read SSE on A and B and the desktop (CDP) and assert identical final transcripts.
2. Approvals: answer from A; B and desktop receive dialog_resolved; a second answer from B gets already_answered.
3. Cancel from B mid-stream; run ends on all.
4. Reconnect: drop A's SSE mid-stream, reconnect with Last-Event-ID, assert no gaps or duplicates; force ring overflow and assert resync path; retry a prompt with the same Idempotency-Key, assert one prompt.
5. Closing A and B mid-run leaves the run going (desktop sees it finish).
6. Load the mobile UI in the test instance's own browser with the iPhone preset and capture screenshots of the slice screens.

Acceptance: the script passes twice in a row; document how to run it in docs/REMOTE.md.
T20_slice_e2e.context: Project: pi-gna (Electron 44 desktop UI for the pi coding agent, macOS; repo /Users/manuelcecchetto/Code/personal/pi-gna). Epic: iPhone remote access: a mobile web app/PWA with feature parity (not identical layout) with the desktop app, used from Safari or the Home Screen over Tailscale (tailscale serve, HTTPS, tailnet only), controlling the pi-gna running on the host Mac. Agents, tools, repositories, the browser and Computer Use stay on the host. Read first: docs/plans/draft/iphone-remote.md (the plan of record: coupling points with file:line evidence, feature inventory, design sections 3.1-3.7, risks, non-goals) and docs/DESIGN.md (architecture, conventions, 'Verifying the UI'). Once T01 exists, docs/REMOTE.md is the contract of record and wins over the plan where they differ. Key decisions: the desktop renderer is NOT rewritten (it keeps IPC and local reduction of events); one HostCore method table in main is dispatched by both IPC and the remote server; orchestration that today lives in the renderer (ATP runner, card/lament/review chat setups, queue ops) moves to Electron main, not to pi extensions (extensions stay for agent-facing tools); the AgentBridge stays loopback-only and is never exposed; no raw RPC passthrough remotely. Constraints: closing or suspending a client never cancels host work; no unauthenticated listener; remote access off by default; never copy host credentials to the phone; no privileged sleep hacks; no native iOS app. Conventions: TypeScript; main and preload import only Node and Electron (no runtime npm dependencies; renderer/mobile code may bundle devDependencies through Vite); pure helpers in src/shared with vitest tests; comment density like surrounding code; update docs/DESIGN.md for behavior changes and add a CHANGELOG.md Unreleased line for user-visible changes. UI checks use test instances exactly as docs/DESIGN.md 'Verifying the UI' says (own PIGNA_USER_DATA, PIGNA_BACKGROUND=1, own free debugging port, scripts/fake-pi.mjs via PIGNA_PI_BIN, stop by PID, never pkill patterns, never touch the user's running pi-gna). ## Outcome
`scripts/remote-slice-e2e.mjs` (`pnpm e2e:remote`) runs the whole remote slice without a phone and passed twice in a row (each run: fresh build into its own folder, fresh instance, 100% of checks). Documented in docs/REMOTE.md ("Automated end-to-end test"). It found and fixed one real defect.

## Facts Learned
- `chat.respondDialog` ignored its caller (host-core passed no ctx), so `dialog_resolved.by` was "desktop" for a phone's answer. Fixed (`callerOf(ctx)`), unit-tested.
- Windows and browser tabs of a PIGNA_BACKGROUND=1 instance draw no frames: `Page.captureScreenshot` hangs (only the first capture after a reload answers) and `webContents.capturePage` on a tab fails with UnknownVizError. An offscreen BrowserWindow created through the inspector (`--inspect`) paints and captures fine.
- The mobile bundle and main must share one PIGNA_BUILD id or the phone sits on "Connecting…" (hello mismatch).
- fake-pi already raised a confirm dialog for prompts containing `ask-confirm`; no extension wrapper was needed. Added `[lines=N]`/`[delay=N]` prompt directives so one instance serves short and long runs.
- The ring overflows after ~2300 events with `[lines=6000][delay=1]` in a few seconds; reconnect then yields `resync` and no replay.
- Pairing a device opens Settings on the desktop window; the script clicks "Back to app" before driving the sidebar.
- A pairing needs no test hook: the window's `studio.remote.pairStart/pairing/pairDecide` over CDP is the Mac's UI path.

## Decisions Made
- No test hook in the app; pairing approval through the window's own API over CDP.
- Transcripts compared as: delta line numbers and final assistant text from SSE events (A, B), the desktop's rendered DOM (last answer lines 1..N once each), and host snapshots; no TS reducer import in the .mjs.
- Screens: offscreen window of the instance (iPhone 15 size, mobile UA, touch emulation) behind a small header-injecting proxy, instead of a browser-pane tab.
- CHANGELOG/DESIGN not edited: both carry other workers' uncommitted ATP edits (committing them would sweep those in).

## Files Touched
scripts/remote-slice-e2e.mjs (new), scripts/fake-pi.mjs, package.json (`e2e:remote`), src/main/host-core.ts (+test), docs/REMOTE.md.

## Interfaces Changed
`chat.respondDialog` now records the caller (`dialog_resolved.by` = device id for remote answers). fake-pi prompt directives `[lines=N]`, `[delay=N]`.

## Verification
- `node scripts/remote-slice-e2e.mjs` twice consecutively: "all checks passed" both times (~85 checks incl. pairing, open/dedupe, approvals first-wins, cancel, Last-Event-ID replay contiguity, idempotent retry, ring overflow resync, clients closing mid-run, 7 mobile screenshots).
- `pnpm typecheck` ok. `pnpm test`: 631 pass, 1 fails: src/main/atp.test.ts "shows a plan the architect writes..." (the known intermittent flake from other workers' uncommitted atp edits, not touched). host-core tests pass (15).

## Risks
- Takes ~4 min and a build; not in `pnpm test`. Uses real timing (fake-pi delays), so a heavily loaded machine could time out some `until` waits (20-60 s budgets).
- Screens are 1x DPR PNGs of an emulated viewport, not a real iOS Safari. Desktop DOM selector (`div[class*="max-w-[800px]"][class*="gap-10"]`) is coupled to the Transcript's classes.
- CHANGELOG Unreleased line and DESIGN.md note still outstanding.

## Recommended Next Step
Add the CHANGELOG/DESIGN lines once the ATP edits are committed; extend the script as attachments/uploads and other screens land (and wire it into a release checklist).
